In what year was Karl Marx born?
Karl Marx: Born in Trier in the Kingdom of Prussia, Marx earned a doctoral degree in philosophy from the University of Jena in 1841.
In what year was Benzene discovered?
Benzene is an organic chemical compound with the molecular formula C6H6.
Perl: Larry Wall. Perl is a high-level, general-purpose, interpreted, dynamic programming language.
IAI Kfir: Israel Aerospace Industries Ltd.
In which country is Thalidomide scandal?
Thalidomide scandal: Germany. It was introduced as a sedative and medication for morning sickness without having been tested on pregnant women.
Who is credited with discovering Flerovium?
Flerovium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Flerovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fl and atomic number 114.
Who is credited with discovering Hypochlorous acid?
Hypochlorous acid: Antoine Jérôme Balard. Hypochlorous acid is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula ClOH, also written as HClO, HOCl, or ClHO.
Who is credited with discovering Gallium?
Gallium: Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran. Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.
A King's College Cambridge graduate who earned a Princeton doctorate in 1938, he later joined Britain's wartime codebreaking effort and pioneered theoretical computing — who was he?
Alan Turing (23 June 1912 - 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher and theoretical biologist.
One of Ptolemy's original 48 and among the largest in the sky, this autumn constellation is named for a mythical princess chained to a rock for the sea monster Cetus — which one?
Andromeda (constellation) is one of the 48 constellations listed by the 2nd-century Greco-Roman astronomer Ptolemy, and one of the 88 modern constellations.

In 2003, this American mountaineer amputated his own trapped forearm with a dull pocket knife after five days pinned by a boulder in a Utah canyon, then rappelled and hiked miles to safety — who is he?

Aron Ralston (born October 27, 1975) is an American mountaineer, mechanical engineer, and motivational speaker, known for surviving a canyoneering accident in 2003 by cutting off part of his own right arm.
Which SI unit of radioactivity honors the scientist who co-discovered the phenomenon alongside the Curies?
Becquerel (symbol: Bq) is the unit of radioactivity in the International System of Units (SI).

Native to eastern North America with resident populations as far north as Newfoundland, this crested songbird in the crow family has a black, U-shaped collar around its neck and a mostly white chest — name it?
Blue jay (Cyanocitta cristata) is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, native to eastern North America.
This flammable, colorless alkane gas with the formula C4H10 takes its name from a Greek word for butter, via butyric acid — what is it?
Butane is an alkane with the formula C4H10. Butane exists as two isomers, n-butane, CH3CH2CH2CH3 and iso-butane, (CH3)3CH.
This root vegetable owes its typical orange color to beta-carotene, though heirloom varieties can be white, purple, or even black — what vegetable is it?
Born in 1847, this American wore three hats at once — psychologist, logician, and mathematician. Who was she?
Christine Ladd-Franklin (December 1, 1847 - March 5, 1930) was an American psychologist, logician, and mathematician.
With algorithms and data structures at its core and the theory of computation among its branches, which field studies computation, information, and automation?

Computer science is the study of computation, information, and automation. The theory of computation concerns abstract models of computation and general classes of problems that can be solved using them.
A law professor known for scholarship on retribution and criminal sentencing, this Harvard-trained academic was killed in 2014 in a murder-for-hire scheme linked to a custody dispute — who is he?

Dan Markel (October 9, 1972 - July 19, 2014) was a Canadian-born attorney and law professor who wrote various works on retribution in criminal law and sentencing with a focus on the role of punishment in the criminal justice system.

England-born but raised in Australia, this geologist did much of his real rock-hunting in the Flinders Ranges — though he's better remembered for braving the ice alongside Shackleton on the Nimrod Expedition; who was he?
Douglas Mawson (5 May 1882 - 14 October 1958) was an Australian geologist, Antarctic explorer, and academic.
This branch of medicine studies the body's hormone-secreting glands and the chemical messengers, called hormones, that regulate growth, metabolism, mood, and more — name the field?
Endocrinology (from endocrine + -ology) is a branch of biology and medicine dealing with the endocrine system, its diseases, and its specific secretions known as hormones.
Every member of this mammal family is an obligate carnivore with retractile claws and a powerful bite, from forest dwellers to desert hunters — which family is it?
Felidae is the family of mammals in the order Carnivora colloquially referred to as cats.
Most common in the hands and feet, this cold-exposure injury can lead to complications like hypothermia or compartment syndrome — what is it called?
Frostbite is an injury to skin or other living tissue that is allowed to freeze, especially affecting the fingers, toes, nose, ears, cheeks and chin.

This small freshwater fish, native to China and one of the world's most popular aquarium pets, has become an invasive pest after being released into wild waterways in North America and Australia — what fish is it?
Goldfish (Carassius auratus) is a freshwater fish in the family Cyprinidae of the order Cypriniformes.
Tapeworms, flukes, and roundworms burrowing into the gut and beyond all fall under this macroparasitic disease — a neglected tropical illness better known as worm infection. What is it?
Helminthiasis is any macroparasitic disease of humans and other animals in which a part of the body is infected with parasitic worms, known as helminths.
Dissolved in water it yields a notoriously corrosive acid, yet it's also the main industrial route to fluorine and a feedstock for Teflon-style polymers like PTFE — which colorless compound is it?
Hydrogen fluoride is an inorganic compound with chemical formula HF.

Acting as the eye's diaphragm in optical terms, this thin ring-shaped structure controls how much light reaches the retina by adjusting the pupil's size, and also determines a person's eye color — name this structure?

Iris (anatomy) (pl.: irides or irises) is a thin, ring-shaped structure in the eye in most mammals and birds that is responsible for controlling the diameter and size of the pupil, and thus the amount of light reaching the retina.

He wrote the first commercial anti-virus software in 1987 and ran twice for the Libertarian presidential nomination — yet later urged people to uninstall the very product that still bears his name. Who is he?
John McAfee (18 September 1945 - 23 June 2021) was a British and American computer programmer, businessman, and two-time U.S.
Endemic to New Zealand, this large, nocturnal, ground-dwelling parrot has owl-like forward-facing eyes and holds the title of the world's only flightless parrot — what bird is it?
Kākāpō (Mori:; pl.: kkp; Strigops habroptilus), sometimes known as the owl-parrot, is a species of large, nocturnal, ground-dwelling parrot of the superfamily Strigopoidea.
Believed to stem from genetic and hormonal disruption of the lymphatic system, this condition traps fat in the legs regardless of a woman's overall weight — what's the diagnosis?
Lipedema is a condition that is almost exclusively found in women and results in enlargement of both legs due to deposits of fat under the skin.
Transmitted by the bite of Anopheles mosquitoes, this infectious disease causes fever, fatigue, and headaches, and in severe cases can lead to seizures, coma, or death — name the disease?
Malaria is a mosquito-borne infectious disease that is transmitted by the bite of Anopheles mosquitoes.
Crushed leaves of this mint-family herb smell like spearmint, yet it has caused deaths when used as a traditional abortifacient — which species, also known as pennyroyal?

Mentha pulegium (European) pennyroyal, or pennyrile, also called mosquito plant and pudding grass, is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae, native to Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East.
In 1812 Étienne Geoffroy grouped the apes with the Cercopithecidae under the name Catarrhini, or "Old World" members of this familiar simian group — what common name is it?
Monkey is a common name that may refer to most mammals of the infraorder Simiiformes, also known as simians.

Encompassing several types of kidney inflammation affecting the glomeruli, tubules, or nearby interstitial tissue, this general medical term falls under the broader category of nephropathy — what's the condition?
Nephritis is inflammation of the kidneys and may involve the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitial tissue surrounding the glomeruli and tubules.
Concerned with the most fundamental concept of all — being — this branch of metaphysics distinguishes non-repeatable particulars from repeatable universals like 'green' — what is the field?
Ontology is the philosophical study of being.
Named for the extra copy of chromosome 13 found in affected cells, this condition — related to Down and Edwards syndromes — disrupts normal organ development — which syndrome?
Patau syndrome is a syndrome caused by a chromosomal abnormality, in which some or all of the cells of the body contain extra genetic material from chromosome 13.
This anxiety disorder involves an irrational, excessive, and persistent fear of a specific object or situation, often leading sufferers to go to great lengths to avoid it — what is it called?
Phobia is an anxiety disorder, defined by an irrational, unrealistic, persistent and excessive fear of an object or situation.
Named from the Greek for an infinite carbon chain it would ultimately become, this class of organic compounds strings together alternating single and triple bonds. What is it called?
Polyyne is any organic compound with alternating single and triple bonds; that is, a series of consecutive alkynes, (CC)n with n greater than 1.

Brought from China to Europe in the sixteenth century and popularized by the House of Orange in the Netherlands, this dog breed is known for its wrinkly, short-muzzled face and curled tail — name the breed?
Pug is a breed of dog with the physically distinctive features of a wrinkly, short-muzzled face, and curled tail.
Also called king's crown or Arctic root, this Arctic-growing perennial is widely sold as a supplement even though regulators say its health claims lack solid evidence — which plant?
Rhodiola rosea (commonly golden root, rose root, roseroot, Aaron's rod, Arctic root, king's crown, lignum rhodium, orpin rose) is a perennial flowering plant in the family Crassulaceae.
Having taught economics at the Catholic University of Asunción and once served as Paraguay's finance minister, this politician assumed his country's presidency in 2023 — who is he?
Santiago Peña (Spanish; born 16 November 1978) is a Paraguayan politician and economist who has served as the 52nd president of Paraguay since 2023.

Defined by the American Thoracic Society as a subjective, uncomfortable experience of breathing discomfort that can include chest tightness or a sense of effort to breathe — what is this sensation called?
Shortness of breath (SOB), known as dyspnea (in AmE) or dyspnoea (in BrE), is an uncomfortable feeling of not being able to breathe well enough.

Distinguished from relatives in its conifer family by four-sided needles attached singly to small peg-like structures on the twigs, this genus of about 37 evergreen tree species thrives across the Northern Hemisphere's boreal forests — what's the tree?

Spruce is a tree of the genus Picea, a genus of some 37 species of coniferous evergreen trees in the family Pinaceae, found in the northern temperate and boreal (taiga) regions of the Northern Hemisphere.
This Turkish businesswoman served as one of her father's chief advisers back in 2013, when he held the office of prime minister and later became Turkey's president — who is she?
Sümeyye Erdoğan (ne Erdoan; born 22 August 1985) is a Turkish businesswoman and the daughter of President Recep Tayyip Erdoan.
Shaped like a butterfly and located in the neck just below the Adam's apple, this endocrine gland's two lobes are joined by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus — name the gland?

Thyroid is an endocrine gland in vertebrates. The lower two thirds of the lobes are connected by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus (pl.: isthmi). The thyroid gland secretes three hormones: the two thyroid hormones – triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4) – and a peptide hormone, calcitonin.

One of the two main forms of inflammatory bowel disease, this long-term condition inflames and ulcerates the colon and rectum, flaring up with abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea before quieting down again — what is it?
Ulcerative colitis (UC) is one of the two types of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), with the other type being Crohn's disease.
Belonging mostly to one family of long-snouted beetles, this group includes bark beetles and grain-damaging pests despite some members lacking the trademark snout — what are they?
Weevil are beetles belonging to the superfamily Curculionoidea, known for their very long snouts.
Also called motor neuron disease or Lou Gehrig's disease, this terminal condition progressively destroys the neurons that control voluntary muscle movement — what is it?
Nicknamed the painted hunter for its mottled coat, this sub-Saharan canine hunts cooperatively at dawn and dusk and is the only living member of its genus, Lycaon — which species?
African wild dog: Species of canine. The African wild dog (Lycaon pictus), also called painted dog and Cape hunting dog, is a wild canine native to sub-Saharan Africa.
Unlike its bulb-forming relative, the common onion, this perennial vegetable never forms a bulb and owes one of its names to its hollow, tube-like leaves — which plant?
Allium fistulosum: Species of plant. The species is very similar in taste and odor to the related common onion, Allium cepa, and hybrids between the two (tree onions) exist.
A branch of morphology with roots in prehistoric times, which natural science studies the internal and external structure of organisms and their parts?
Anatomy: Study of the structure of organisms. Anatomy is a branch of natural science that deals with the structural organization of living things.
Commonly called a canker sore, this recurring condition produces benign mouth ulcers that heal within 7 to 10 days but often return three to six times a year — what is it?
Aphthous stomatitis: Common oral condition lasting 7–10 days.
One of the oldest of the natural sciences, it leans on math, physics, and chemistry to explain everything from comets to quasars beyond Earth's atmosphere — what field is this?
Astronomy: Scientific study of celestial objects.
Also called Asian sea bass, this catadromous fish is widely distributed from the Middle East across South and Southeast Asia to Oceania — which fish?
Barramundi: Species of fish. The species is widely distributed in the Indo-West Pacific, spanning the waters of the Middle East, South Asia, Southeast Asia, East Asia, and Oceania.
This field covers physiological traits like fingerprints and iris patterns, plus behavioral ones like typing rhythm and gait, all used to identify people — what is it called?
Biometrics: Metrics related to human characteristics.
Also known as the penny bun or porcino, this prized edible fungus can grow a brown cap up to a foot wide and forms symbiotic partnerships with forest tree roots — which mushroom?
Boletus edulis: Species of mushroom, widely distributed in the Northern Hemisphere.
Bred in the 19th century as a guard dog by crossing the English Mastiff with the now-extinct Old English Bulldog, which large, short-muzzled English breed was recognized by the Kennel Club in 1924?
Bullmastiff: English breed of dog. The Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.
This Sicilian pastry is a fried, tube-shaped shell filled with sweet ricotta, dressed up with candied orange zest in Palermo or chopped pistachios in Catania — what treat is it?
Cannoli: Italian ricotta-filled pastry. Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
Native to the western Himalayas and the Mediterranean's high altitudes, this coniferous genus bears erect cones and wood that naturally repels moths — which genus?
Native to the high Andes and living in colonies called 'herds,' this South American rodent boasts the densest fur of any land mammal — about 20,000 hairs per square centimeter. What is it?
Chinchilla: Rodent genus. The chinchilla is named after the Chincha people of the Andes, who once wore its dense, velvet-like fur and ate its meat.
With a coat of dusky-grey blotches that inspired its common name, this wild cat is one of the few able to climb down tree trunks head-first, using a long tail for balance — what species is it?

Clouded leopard: Species of wild cat. Its head-and-body length ranges from 68.6 to 108 cm (27.0 to 42.5 in) with a 61 to 91 cm (24 to 36 in) long tail, which it uses for balancing when moving in trees.

Native to the western Palearctic and closely related to the rock dove, this large bird feeds mainly on cereals and other plant matter, making it an agricultural pest despite being heavily hunted across its range — what is it?
Common wood pigeon: Species of large, white/green-naped, arboreal bird of Eurasia.
Usually viral and often worse at night, this childhood respiratory infection swells the trachea and announces itself with an unmistakable barking, brassy cough — what's it called?
Croup: Respiratory infection often caused by a virus.

Nicknamed the 'Wooden Wonder' for its mostly-timber airframe, this WWII British warplane was among the fastest operational aircraft of 1941 and later moonlighted as a high-speed courier for a national airline — what was it?
De Havilland Mosquito: British multi-role combat aircraft of WW2.
This American social platform carries text, media and video, plus voice calls delivered over the internet using which technology?
Discord is an American instant messaging and VoIP social platform allowing communication through voice calls, video calls, text messaging and media, privately or in communities.
This social science splits into a 'micro' branch studying individual agents and markets and a 'macro' branch treating whole economies as systems of production and consumption — what's the field?
Economics: Social science studying goods and services.
Since the 1960s, growing movements have pushed governments to restrain activities that damage the natural world and its resources — what is this broad field of effort called?
Environmental protection: Practice of protecting the natural environment.
Sporting pinkish-brown plumage, a black tail and a flash of bright blue on the wing, this woodland member of the crow family ranges from western Europe to the Indian subcontinent — which bird?
Eurasian jay: Species of bird. It has pinkish brown plumage with a black stripe on each side of a whitish throat, a bright blue panel on the upper wing and a black tail.
This anaerobic metabolic process, used by humans to preserve and flavor food for some 13,000 years, breaks down sugars to generate ATP when oxygen is scarce — what's it called?
Fermentation: Metabolic redox process producing energy in the absence of oxygen.
This American physician-scientist led the Human Genome Project before directing the NIH for over a decade under three presidents — who guided the mapping of our DNA?

Born as an air-superiority day fighter and now, as of 2026, the world's most common military fixed-wing aircraft with over 4,600 built, this single-engine jet flies on as the 'Viper' family — which aircraft?
General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon: American multi-role fighter aircraft.
Bred at a Scottish estate by crossing a flat-coated gun dog with Tweed Water Spaniels, this gentle, honey-coated working dog was recognized by the Kennel Club in 1913 — which breed?
Golden Retriever: Scottish breed of dog. It is characterised by a gentle and affectionate nature and a striking golden coat.
Caused by a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens, which benign condition results in enlarged breast tissue in men?
Gynecomastia: Enlargement of the human male breast.

This French mathematician, famous for his work in algebraic topology, came from an almost absurdly mathematical dynasty: son of mathematician Élie, nephew of mathematician Anna, and brother to a composer, a physicist, and yet another mathematician — who was he?
This small rodent, pointed-snouted with large rounded ears, has become the standard laboratory model organism after thriving alongside human settlements — what is it?
Apple's proprietary mobile operating system, originally called iPhone OS, was unveiled in January 2007 alongside which product?
iOS, formerly iPhone OS, is a proprietary mobile operating system created by Apple for its iPhone line. It was unveiled in January 2007 alongside the first-generation iPhone and released that June.
This condition restricts blood flow to tissue, starving cells of oxygen and nutrients due to causes like thrombosis or embolism — what's it called?
Ischemia: Restriction in blood supply to tissues.
As chief engineer, this man designed the Mitsubishi A6M Zero, Japan's iconic World War II fighter plane, and later worked on the postwar NAMC YS-11 airliner — who is he?

Caused by a herpesvirus and linked to weakened immunity such as HIV/AIDS, this cancer produces purple skin lesions and disproportionately affects older Mediterranean men in its 'classic' form — which condition?
Kaposi's sarcoma: Cancer of the skin, integumentary lymph nodes, or other organs.
This reddish-brown, bitter tincture dissolved opium poppy extract in alcohol and was once sold without a prescription as a cough and pain remedy — what is it?
Laudanum: Tincture of opium. Laudanum is a tincture of opium containing approximately 10% powdered opium by weight (the equivalent of 1% morphine).
Native to the Indo-Pacific, this venomous aquarium favorite sports red-and-black banded warning colors and ostentatious spiny fins, and has become an invasive nightmare in the Caribbean — what is it?
Named from the Latin for "wolf," this autoimmune disease often announces itself with a red facial rash and alternates between flares and remission — what is it?
Lupus: Autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks healthy tissue.
Dubbed "sea locusts" by the ancient Assyrians and "prawn killers" by others, these burrow-dwelling crustaceans are among the most important predators of shallow tropical seas. What are they?
Mantis shrimp: Order of crustaceans. Mantis shrimp are carnivorous marine crustaceans of the order Stomatopoda (from Ancient Greek στόμα (stóma) 'mouth' and πούς (poús) 'foot').

Element 101, first made in 1955 by bombarding einsteinium with alpha particles, was the first that couldn't be produced by simply neutron-blasting a lighter element — and it honors the father of the periodic table. Which element is it?
Mendelevium: Chemical element with atomic number 101 (Md)

An advanced modification of its Korean War-era predecessor, this Soviet transonic fighter — NATO reporting name 'Fresco' — was license-built in China and Poland, and remains in North Korean service today — which jet?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17: Soviet jet fighter aircraft family.

Prized by gourmet cooks yet toxic if eaten raw or undercooked, this genus of honeycomb-capped edible fungi is difficult to cultivate, making wild harvests a multimillion-dollar industry — which fungal genus?
Morchella: Genus of fungi. Morchella, the true morels, is a genus of edible sac fungi closely related to anatomically simpler cup fungi in the order Pezizales (division Ascomycota).
Sold as Narcan, this opioid antagonist can restore breathing within minutes of an overdose but may trigger sudden withdrawal in opioid-dependent people — what is it?
Naloxone: Opioid receptor antagonist. Naloxone, sold under the brand name Narcan among others, is an opioid antagonist, a medication used to reverse or reduce the effects of opioids.
Colourless and odourless, this element pairs with itself to form a diatomic gas that makes up about 78% of the air you're breathing — what is it?
Nitrogen: Chemical element with atomic number 7 (N)

The most widely cultivated species of its genus, this bulb vegetable counts garlic, leeks and chives among its close relatives, and the shallot was reclassified as merely a variety of it in 2011 — what is it?
Onion: Bulbous vegetable. The shallot is a botanical variety of the onion which was classified as a separate species until 2011.
Nicknamed the 'scaly anteater,' this nocturnal mammal is covered in keratin scales and slurps up ants and termites with a long tongue — which animal?
Pangolin: Mammals of the order Pholidota.
Developed at Abbott Laboratories in 1930 and nicknamed 'yellow jackets' for its brand-name capsule color, this barbiturate is used in veterinary euthanasia and some U.S. executions — what drug is it?
Cultivated since the days of the Inca Empire and known in English as the Cape gooseberry or goldenberry, this South American nightshade now grows wild worldwide — which species is it?
Physalis peruviana: Species of cultivated South American fruit. Physalis peruviana is a species of plant in the nightshade family (Solanaceae) native to Chile and Peru.
Most commonly referring to a type called PET, this category of polymers built from ester linkages is often blended with cotton to reduce wrinkling — what is it called?
Polyester: Category of polymers, in which the monomers are joined together by ester links.
This Old World tree species has two main cultivar groups, the dark-red Morello and the lighter Amarelle, prized for their tart, edible pulp — which fruit-bearing plant?
Prunus cerasus: Species of cherry tree. Prunus cerasus (sour cherry, tart cherry, or dwarf cherry) is an Old World species of Prunus in the subgenus Cerasus (cherries).
A small herbivore of the family Leporidae and a cousin to hares, this prey animal has been introduced to every continent except Antarctica — what is it?
Rabbit: Mammals of the family Leporidae. The most widespread rabbit genera are Oryctolagus and Sylvilagus.
Responsible for at least half of all common colds, this tiny RNA virus in the Picornaviridae family measures only about 30 nanometers across — what is it?
Discovered in 1844 by Karl Ernst Claus and named in honor of Russia, which unreactive platinum-group element with atomic number 44 now caps extreme ultraviolet photomasks for chip lithography?
Ruthenium: Chemical element with atomic number 44 (Ru)
Named from Greek words for 'thorn' and 'earthworm,' which genus of large tropical centipedes gives its name to an entire family of segmented, many-legged predators?
Named for its enormous footwear-shaped beak, this large wading bird of East African swamps was once classified with storks but is now grouped with pelicans and herons — what is it?
Shoebill: Species of bird. The shoebill (Balaeniceps rex), also known as the whale-headed stork, whalebill, and shoe-billed stork, is a large long-legged wading bird.
After designing the BBC Micro and its BASIC, this English computer scientist co-created the instruction set for ARM — now the most widely used processor architecture in smartphones. Who is she?

Striking about one in a million people, this rare neurological disorder brings progressive muscular rigidity and spasms that twist the trunk into postural deformities — first described in 1956, what is it?
Stiff-person syndrome: Neurological disorder. The stiffness primarily affects the truncal muscles and is characterised by spasms, resulting in postural deformities.

This red-orange, sublimable heterocyclic solid is a stable aminoxyl radical used as a spin probe in electron spin resonance spectroscopy and as a mediator in controlled radical polymerization — what's this compound commonly called?

This geometry rule holds that a triangle inscribed in a circle, with one side running through the center as a diameter, always has a right angle at its third point — proved by Euclid, though occasionally miscredited to Pythagoras. What's it called?
Thales's theorem: On triangles inscribed in a circle with a diameter as an edge.
Called the "Father of Japanese Botany," this grammar-school dropout collected over 500,000 plant specimens and earned a doctorate — and his birthday is now Botany Day in Japan. Who was he?
Also known as 45,X, which chromosomal condition affects only females who are born with a single X chromosome instead of two, often causing short stature and a webbed neck?
Turner syndrome: X chromosome monosomy. Small chin (micrognathia), loose folds of skin on the neck, slanted eyelids and prominent ears are found in Turner syndrome, though not all will show it.
Also called vervain, this genus of roughly 150 flowering plant species is native mostly to the Americas and Asia, though its European type species grows wild there too — what genus is it?
Verbena: Genus of plants. Verbena, also known as vervain or (in obsolete spelling) verveine, is a genus in the family Verbenaceae.

With black-tipped wings and long red legs and bill, this long-distance migrant famously avoids the open Mediterranean, detouring instead via Gibraltar or the Levant on its way to African wintering grounds — which bird is it?
White stork: Species of bird. The white stork (Ciconia ciconia) is a large bird in the stork family, Ciconiidae.
Marketed under the brand name Imovane, this 'Z-drug' sedative treats insomnia by boosting GABA activity in the brain much like a benzodiazepine, though it's chemically distinct — what is it?
The symbol for phosphorus is P. Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.

In what year was Cher born?
Cher (SHAIR; legally mononymous; born Cheryl Sarkisian, May 20, 1946) is an American singer and actress.
In what year was Olga Kurylenko born?
Olga Kurylenko: Olga Kostyantynivna Kurylenko (born 14 November 1979) is a Ukrainian-born French actress and former model.
In what year was Gal Gadot born?
Gal Gadot (Hebrew: גל גדות, pronounced [ˈɡal ɡaˈdot]; born 30 April 1985) is an Israeli actress.
In what year was Lily-Rose Depp born?
Lily-Rose Depp: Lily-Rose Melody Depp (born May 27, 1999) is a French and American actress and singer.
In what year was Fran Drescher born?
Fran Drescher: Francine Joy Drescher (born September 30, 1957) is an American actress, writer, comedian, producer, and former trade union leader.
In what year was Chuck Norris born?
Chuck Norris: Carlos Ray "Chuck" Norris (March 10, 1940 – March 19, 2026) was an American martial artist, actor, screenwriter, and author.
In what year was Prabhas born?
Prabhas made his acting debut with the drama Eeswar (2002) and later attained his breakthrough with the action romance Varsham (2004).
In what year was George Lucas born?
